sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Hall County
sections.html:
Two Gainesville offices split the work. The Board of Assessors sets the value of your property. The Tax Commissioner mails the statements and takes payment. Neither office sets the rate. Mill levies are voted by the county commissioners, the school board and each city that taxes on its own.

Gainesville is the county seat. Most of the county sits in the Hall County School District, while parcels inside the city limits of Buford and Gainesville fall under those cities' own school systems, which changes the millage that applies. Check which district your address is in before you compare your bill with a neighbor's.

  • Assessment questions: Board of Assessors, 2875 Browns Bridge Road, Gainesville, 770.531.6720 for real property.
  • Billing and payment questions: Tax Commissioner, 770.531.6950 option 3, open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • City bills: owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood receive a second statement from that city.

Sixty days after mailing is the rule in Hall. A normal season means a September 15 mailing and a November 15 deadline. The 2026 statements went out October 15, a month late because the state approval of the digest came late, so the deadline became December 15, 2026.

The 60 day gap stays fixed even when the mailing slips, so a later bill gives you a later deadline. Interest starts building monthly once the deadline passes. Plan around the date printed on your own statement.

Ways to pay a Hall County bill
Payment methodCost or location
E-Check at HallCountyTax.orgFlat $1.50
Credit card2.49%
Debit card1.50%
Mail the pay slipP.O. Box 1579, Gainesville, GA 30503
Drop boxUnder the breezeway at the Government Center, Browns Bridge Road, open 24 hours

The online portal shows payment status for every parcel and keeps records and receipts for the past ten years. You can also pay by phone with a card.

Paying before the deadline also keeps a clean record for the title company when you list. Save the receipt from the portal and give a copy to your closing attorney.

You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Hall takes appeals three ways: online in qPublic, by post to P.O. Box 2895, Gainesville, GA 30503, or at the counter at 2875 Browns Bridge Road.

If you do nothing in that window, the value goes to the Tax Commissioner for billing. Notices are mailed to every owner each year, and the 2026 digital copies were posted on qPublic.

An appeal never freezes the bill. Hall County sends an Under Appeal statement for the 2026 cycle, and the amount due by December 15, 2026 is the lower result of 85% of the 2026 value or 100% of the 2025 value. Any unpaid portion still accrues monthly interest from that date. A refund after a final appeal decision is processed automatically. Other refund claims for erroneous or illegal taxes must start within three years of payment.

Filing season runs January 1 through April 1. Homestead applications, real property returns and personal property returns all use that window, and most of it can be done online through qPublic.

  • Homestead exemptions, including the senior exemptions, the Total School Tax Exemption and the 100% Disabled Veteran exemption, are filed under the Real Property tab in qPublic.
  • Boats, personal watercraft, aircraft, business personal property and manufacturer personal property returns go under the Personal Property tab. Returns filed after April 1 carry a 10% late filing penalty.
  • Conservation Use covenants are taken in person at the Government Center, where an appointment is advised.

You can apply any time once the house is your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of relief. A missed homestead filing is treated as a waiver for that year. Call 770.531.6720 about real property or 770.531.6749 about personal property.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Hall County house sells?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner of record is answerable for that year's tax, even when the house changes hands in spring or summer. Who actually pays is a closing-table question, and the closing attorney handles it.

Hall County adds a step that sellers should not skip. If you sold real property during 2026, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the due date, which works out to March 15, 2027. When the documents clearly shift liability to the new owner, the seller is no longer billed. Papers that arrive after March 15, 2027 cannot be considered. Boats, planes and business fixtures work the same way: whoever owned them in January stays on the hook after a sale.

If you have an escrow account, the county passes tax data to your mortgage servicer, yet the owner still answers for payment.

Before you list, ask the Tax Commissioner what your parcel owes and hand that number to the closing attorney. Unpaid balances carry monthly interest after the deadline, and a buyer's title company will want them cleared at closing.

  1. Call 770.531.6950 option 3 and ask for the current balance on the parcel.
  2. Confirm whether a city bill also exists for your address.
  3. Bring the payoff figure to the closing attorney so it can come out of your proceeds.
  4. After the sale, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027 if the sale happened in 2026.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which can shorten the stretch in which a bill might come due mid-contract. The tax rules above still apply to whoever owned the house on January 1.

Population is 226,568 as of July 1, 2025, up 11.7% since the April 2020 count. A typical owned home is valued at $350,400 for 2020 to 2024, household income is $80,901 and monthly rent is $1,341.

The county has 86,917 housing units and 73,551 households, and 68.6% of homes are owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,742 a month on housing, while owners with none spend $550. The 1,996 building permits issued in 2025 point to steady new construction, which gives resale buyers plenty of competing choices. Price your house with that supply in mind, and have the tax balance settled so it does not slow an offer.

faqs.q: When do 2026 Hall County property taxes have to be paid?
faqs.a: The 2026 bills are due December 15, 2026. They were mailed October 15, and the due date stays at 60 days after mailing. In a typical year the statements go out September 15 and fall due November 15.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Hall County valuation?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 45 days after the date on the notice. After that, the value moves on to billing. Use qPublic, the P.O. Box 2895 mailing address, or the counter on Browns Bridge Road.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hall County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. HallCountyTax.org accepts E-Check for a flat $1.50, PayPal, and cards at 2.49% for credit and 1.50% for debit. You can also mail a check, use the Government Center drop box, or call 770.531.6950 to pay by card.

faqs.q: Who is billed for 2026 if my Hall County house sells?
faqs.a: The January 1, 2026 owner of record owes that year's tax, and the closing documents decide who actually pays. To move billing to the buyer, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027.

faqs.q: Do Hall County cities send their own tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood get a separate city statement in addition to the county bill. The county bill covers county and school levies only.
